Let's look at the signals necessary for the connection of the IO to the 8051. The graphic below shows only the pins used to connect the 8051 microcontroller to the IO..he IO. the IO.
Many of the signals are the same as those used by the memory circuits. The differences are in the instructions that have to be used to access IO circuitry......circuitry.

Unlike many other microcontroller or microprocessor systems, there is no specific command for IO devices connected in this manner. Instead, they interface similar to the way RAM is connected to the system.. the system. the system.e system.

Each address combination of the 8051 address lines can be used by memory or a device attached to the system. Most devices will take a range of addresses, not just one. These different addresses use different functions of the device.he device.he device.....evice.

Now that you understand the basic connection of IO circuits, which is very similar to memory connections, let's look at different devices connected to the 8051. to the 8051.the 8051.
There are two types of IO devices, fixed or removable. IO Devices Fixed Removable Input Input Output Output Input/Output Input/Output
Examples of fixed IO's are the 8051 keyboard and display. Fixed IO devices are permanently connected to the system. system.

Removable IO devices are connected to a microcontroller through a special universal connection port. These ports are designed for many different types of IO devices. Removable IO's such as: a digital camera, Nida test console, mouse, printer, or scanner, would be connected to either the parallel or serial port of the 8051 microcontroller.icrocontroller.roller.crocontroller.ocontroller.ontroller.
IO devices fall into one of three categories: Input, Output, or Input/Output. Let's look at an example of each to understand how they communicate with the microcontroller..ontroller..

Input devices allow information to be sent to the microcontroller or to control it in some fashion. A keyboard, for example, can be used to select options, program new instructions, or even make modifications to old programs.. Mouse Lightpen Trackball Scanner Keyboardd KeyboardKeyboardeyboard
Input devices include: a mouse, lightpen, trackball, scanner or keyboard, to name a few. The only "Input Only" device on the 8051 microcontroller trainer is the keyboard...ypad.keypad.

Input means that the device does not provide any outputs to the user. To better understand the operation of an input device, let's look at the actual circuitry used to control the keyboard in the 8051 microcontroller system.. system.system.er system.
We will begin by looking at a block diagram of the system and, as each section is covered, the blocks will be replaced by their actual circuitry.cuitry.circuitry.

MATRIXTT

As you can see, the keyboard has been broken down into five main sections: control, keyboard latch, keyboard matrix, keyboard buffer, and the key decoding circuit. Let's start by looking at the keyboard key matrix. matrix. matrix.
KEY DECODING CIRCUIT
The keyboard matrix is an arrangement of horizontal and vertical wires with switches connected across them. Pressing any one key connects two wires, one horizontal and one vertical....al.rtical.
KEYBOARD

Each key has its own unique connection so that the microcontroller can differentiate one key from another. By sending a signal through a vertical wire, the horizontal wires can be looked at to see which key in that row was pressed, if any. This brings us to the next circuit, the keyboard latch....latch.d latch.d latch.ad latch...

The keyboard latch is an 8-bit latch connected to the 8 vertical connections of the keyboard key matrix. The output of a latch is the last input present when the clock signal triggered the latch. latch. latch.

The data bus of the 8051 is used to send and receive signals from the keyboard circuitry. Since we cannot send and receive at the same time, a latch provides a way of keeping a previous set of signals from the data bus, allowing results of these applied signals to be read. read. read.. read. read...

A program in the microcontroller sets the latch to output all highs to all the vertical lines. The program then waits to see if an interrupt is generated by the key decoding circuit as a result of a key being pressed...

If an interrupt is not generated, the system will not need to perform any actions regarding the keyboard. When an interrupt signal is generated, the system will respond to the keyboard. It is important to note that the keyboard circuitry may be different than others you have learned about.out..about..learned about. about.bout...
This keyboard could be implemented without using an interrupt. In this scheme, the controller would have to constantly poll the keyboard circuit to see if there is any information there.
The keyboard used in this experiment uses an interrupt to notify the microcontroller that a key has been pressed, thus no polling is necessary.e. information.ation.

The three horizontal lines of the keyboard matrix are connected to the first three inputs of the keyboard buffer. Notice that each of the three lines are connected to GND through a resistor.....resistor.
KEY DECODING CIRCUIT
When none of the keys are being pressed on the keyboard, there is a LOW signal on each of thehorizontal lines. This is because ground is connected to each line through a resistor..or. resistor.

If a key is pressed on a row where the vertical line is LOW, then a LOW will be connected to the associated horizontal line and to the buffer. This condition causes an unrecognizable keystroke which cannot be identified by the microcontroller...ler.roller...troller.
If a key is pressed on a row where the vertical line is HIGH, then a HIGH will be connected to the resistor and to the buffer.r.buffer.
Since all the vertical lines are HIGH, any key pressed will cause a HIGH on one of the buffer inputs. In this situation, you cannot tell which column the key you pressed was in.as in.was in.

Pressing a key generates an interrupt signal in the key decoding circuit. The microcontroller is very fast. For this reason, when you press a key, an interrupt signal in the key decoding circuit is generated. When a key is pressed for a fraction of a second the microcontroller reads the generated signal hundreds of times..f times.s of times..times. of times.

After key-press notification, the microcontroller sets all of the vertical lines LOW and then places a HIGH, one line at a time, on each vertical line while it determines which key was pressed. This operation occurs a minimum of 10 times per second, so your finger will probably still be on the key long after the microcontroller has determined what key was pressed...ddd

It is important to note that the microcontroller only allows one vertical line to be HIGH at a time. This means that when a key is pressed, it can only detect one key. key...........................................................................

The key decoding circuit, as shown below, only allows the microcontroller to register the pressed key once before generating the needed interrupt signal. While the key is being held down it doesn't allow its circuits to reset... to reset..o reset.reset.

The two OR gates are attached in a way that when a key is pressed, the output goes HIGH. This high signal is referred to as the KP or key pressed signal. While the key is pressed, a HIGH is applied to the CLK input of the first flip-flop, U4A.....stor capacitor pair before connecting to the flip-flop pair.

This HIGH causes the Q output to go HIGH and the Q to go LOW of flip-flop U4A. This applies a HIGH to the D input and a LOW to the reset pin of the second flip-flop, U4B.ce the set pin of the first flip-flop has been set high for a short amount of time, Q goes high and Q goes low. This applies a HIGH to the D input of flip-flop 2 and a low to the reset pin of flip flop two.

The Q signal is also sent to the microcontroller INT0 pin. This means that a key press is detected by interrupt. If no interrupt occurs within a specific range of time, the microcontroller assumes no key was pressed...nterrupt occurs within a specific range of time, the microcontroller assumes no key was pressed..pressed..ed.sed.

When a key is pressed and an interupt signal is recognized, the microcontroller begins searching for the pressed key. It then reads the key from the data bus using the appropriate signals needed for accessing the keyboard.

When a key is read, the control section provides a signal which resets the flip-flops so they will be ready for the next key. ote that if the resistor/capacitor circuit wasn't there and you pressed a key, the circuit would not be able to reset.....eset.set.to reset.
Remember, the circuit could effectively detect your key press more than 100 times in a single second. It is very important to make sure it only detects once. once.cts once.

The control section is the last section of the keyboards circuits. This circuit is regulated by the microcontroller and oversees all sections of the keyboard circuit. The three signals applied to the control circuit are: RD, KB, and WR................ry.try.

These signals determine if the circuit is to read, write, or remain inactive. The output of the microcontroller's IO chip select circuitry is connected to the keyboard control circuit. This way, only the keyboard will be active when the microcontroller is reading or writing data to this device........................................................................................

The IO chip select can select other devices like the LCD and other IO connections. IO uses the same memory addresses as the EPROM, however, the EPROM is accessed as program memory and IO is accessed as external data..al data.ternal data.nal data.

While input devices allow you to input information into a microcontroller system, output devices allow you to see or receive feedback from the microcontroller about operations, data, or performance.. Printer Display Monitorrr Monitor Monitor
An output device could be a printer or display of some sort. Many microcontroller systems like the 8051 have outputs to monitors, or LCD displays.CD displays. displays.
To get a better understanding of output devices, let's look at the operation of the LCD display of the 8051 microcontroller system. LCD Circuitry LCD Circuitryrcuitry

LCD is an acronym which stands for Liquid Crystal Display, which also describes the technique of how the display works. A liquid crystal display has an actual liquid crystal in between two pieces of glass.f glass. of glass. of glass...

Transparent, conductive materials are used to apply voltage to the liquid crystal. When voltage is applied, the crystals in the liquid scatter and do not allow light to pass through the glass. glass.he glass.
In the rear portion of the glass, holding the liquid crystal, a reflective surface shines light backwards through the glass illuminating the characters.ters.

The LCD unit, like the one on the PC130-406 card, has fourteen pins interfacing the LCD unit with the NIDA 8051 microcontroller system. The graphic shows the signals of the LCD display module.. module. module.

Vss and Vdd are used to power the LCD module. Vcc is used to set the intensity of the display. You can see that this pin is connected to a potentiometer with one side connected to 5 volts and the other to ground.round. ground.ground...

Adjusting the potentiometer will adjust the display intensity. The next three connections of the LCD module are control lines. The control lines are the RS (Register Select), R/W (Read/Not Write) and the E (Enable) pins...) pins.ble) pins.) pins.

There are two types of memory within the display unit: character memory and display memory. Character memory holds all the information about the displayable characters and the user definable characters..acters. characters.characters...

User definable characters means that you can assign them to whatever function you want. Character memory is split into two sections: RAM and ROM. The character RAM, also known as the CG RAM, holds all of the user defined character codes.er codes.r codes..codes.

If you create your own characters you must reload them into the display every time you turn the display module on. This is because CG memory space is RAM and is erased when power is removed from the system............................................... system. system.he system.

The character ROM, known as the CG ROM, holds all the permanent information about the predefined unchangeable characters of the display module. Data books written about the displays will illustrate the predefined characters, how they are organized, and also indicate which characters can be changed..changed.s can be changed. be changed. be changed...
The display RAM, known as the DD RAM, is used to hold the current information that is being displayed on the LCD screen. There isn't any DD ROM because it isn't necessary.ecessary.necessary.
All areas of the screen are fully programmable. The last eight lines of the display module connections are data lines. These lines are used to input information to the display module...dule.dule.
Now that we have looked at the input and output devices, let's look at some common circuits which employ both methods of communication, input and output..output. output.

The potentiometer in the LCD circuitry does what?djusts the speed of characters displayed on the screen. . .usts the intensity of the characters displayed on the LCD.ty of the characters displayed on the LCD. the LCD. the LCD. the LCD...
Adjusts the speed of characters displayed on the screen.
Turns the volume of the speaker up or down.
Adjusts the intensity of the characters displayed on the LCD.

The potentiometer is used to control the intensity of the characters on the LCD display. There is no speaker in the LCD unit and the speed of characters being displayed is determined by the microcontroller. microcontroller.ocontroller.roller...

The two most common forms of input/output are the serial and parallel ports. Ports are connectors in a system used to interface external devices. External devices could be modems, printers, scanners, etc... INPUT/OUTPUT SERIAL PORT PARALLEL PORTLLEL PORTLEL PORTALLEL PORT
INPUT/OUTPUT
PARALLEL PORT

An I/O port allows you to hook up any of these using a standardized protocol, either serial or parallel. There are other types of standard connections, however, we are only discussing the types implemented in the Nida 8051 system.051 system.a 8051 system. system...
INPUT/OUTPUT
SERIAL PORTORTL PORT

The names serial and parallel describe the type of communication that occurs. Serial connections only require, at a minimum, three connections for two-way communication. Send, receive and ground.nd ground.and ground.

In some systems more connections are provided for certain types of control and protection, however, in most cases these types of signals aren't needed. Serial indicates that, at any given time, only one data bit can be sent...be sent.t can be sent. be sent...

If you were sending 8-bits of data, it would take 8 sends to completely transmit the bits. The advantage of serial communications is that it only requires a few wires, so it's well adapted for telephone. telephone..phone.e...
PARALLEL PORT
PARALLEL PORT CONNECTIONS

Parallel communication, used mostly with printers, is the sending of many bits at once. Normally, 8-bits are sent each on their own line. Additional lines are also provided for control and protection.tion.ection...

The parallel port is faster than the serial port because of thie simultaneous transfer of data. This increased speed, however, comes at a cost. Increased cost for multiple conductor cable, more complex required circuitry, and signal degradation as cable lengths increase, all combine to limit the length of parallel data cables to lengths shorter than serial data cables.. , however, the cable lengths used to connect to a parallel port are shorter. Printers are commonly right next to your computer. For this reason the parallel port is used.

Frequently, printers are located close to the computer making the use of the parallel port for interconnection ideal. On some systems the parallel port is called the printer port, on others it is called LPT.

In some situations, certain devices need the speed of the parallel port and the distance of the serial port. Special devices exist that can amplify and boost the signal of the parallel port to allow it to travel longer distances.gnal of the parallel port to allow it to travel longer distances..ces.ances.istances.istances...

In the 8051 system, the parallel and serial port are actually built into the 8051 microcontroller. Unlike many other systems, this reduces the number of external chips and connections..tions.ons.

Additionally, this frees up external IO address connections that, in other systems, are used to connect external parallel and serial IO devices. This is one of the reasons the 8051 is such an ideal choice for many applications..ations.ications.ations.

In this experiment, we are going to observe signals of the keyboard in two states: when no key is being pressed, and when a key is being pressed.ssed.. pressed.essed and when a key is being pressed.
The operation is important in both conditions. By looking at the signals of these two states of operation we can see the operation of the circuit.. circuit.circuit.
You will use the oscilloscope during this lesson to view waveforms that may or may not be periodic. When viewing these types of waveforms, you have two possibilities of observation.tion....
OSCILLOSCOPE
HORIZONTAL

The first type of signals are the periodic type. The oscilloscope's hold-off and triggering level controls are useful for acquiring the correct presentation.icrocontroller and keypad circuitry..ry.cuitry.
You will also measure signals when you press keys on the keyboard. The signals are not periodic and your goal is to at least observe some sort of change in the signal.signal.the signal.
The signals are not easily viewed, but some observation can be made that something is occurring in the system.he system.
9. Connect CH1 of the oscilloscope to the X1 through X8 test points of PC130-405 one by one..e by one.
These are the vertical connections to the keyboard matrix. Notice all eight of these signals are high. Remember that these signals remain HIGH while waiting for a key to be pressed.sed.pressed.
If a key in any row is pressed, a high will be applied to one of the inputs of the two connected OR gates which will generate an interrupt to the microcontroller.controller.er.
10. Connect CH1 of the oscilloscope to the TPB2 INT0 test point of PC130-405.................. PC130-405.

This is one of the interrupt inputs to the microcontroller. The signal is steady at +5V. Since there is an interrupt when a LOW is applied to an interrupt pin, there are no interrupts being generated by the keyboard decoding circuitry at this time. This should make sense since no key is being pressed....pressed.ed.
11. Observe the oscilloscope display while CH1 of the oscilloscope is connected to the INT0 test point, and press the "9" key on the 8051 keyboard. 8051 keypad.

You should observe a flicker in the display. When the key was pressed, the keyboard decoding circuitry applied the input to the flip-flop which, through other circuitry, generated the interrupt signal that you observed.....ved.bserved.bserved.
12. Connect CH1 of the oscilloscope to the KP test point of PC130-406..
The signal should be low. This is the output of the two OR gates which connect to all three horizontal key connections. This signal indicates when a key is being pressed..ressed. pressed.
13. Observe the oscilloscope display while CH1 of the oscilloscope is connected to the KP test point, and press the "9" key on the 8051 keyboard.51 keypad.
While the key was pressed down, the signal observed at the KP test point should be high. This stays high while the key is pressed down.ed down.

It is this signal that, when applied to clock input of flip-flop U4A, generates the interrupt signal, INT0.us for a short amount of time to the interrupt generation circuit of the key decoding circuit.circuit.

What you have seen are the important signals used with the keyboard circuitry of the 8051 Microcontroller system. Being able to recognize proper system operation and changes in signals is important in analyzing the operation of the system..of the system. of the system.the system.

There are many other signals in the keyboard circuit, unfortunately they are difficult to observe in any useful form. For instance, there is a WR signal asserted every time the voltages change on the horizontal lines of the keyboard matrix, also, the RD line is asserted when the current key press is being read into the system..........ystem. system.em.e system.
When you get to troubleshooting the 8051 microcontroller, it will be important to remember and understand the signal conditions in the system. system.system.
While you may not be able to exactly determine if the WR signal is being asserted at the proper time, you will be able to verify its presence.ence.presence. its presence.
These kinds of observations are very important. Opens in a system can cause all sorts of problems.problems.
